recommendation: Keep the no-change audit for core. If the PA admin-incubator operation pages are reconciled separately, verify that their Patient/Encounter $everything definitions continue to preserve the same _since record-time semantics.
issue_request: FHIR-13921 was a Published FHIR-core change request with resolution Persuasive with Modification. It asked that $everything explicitly document periodic update queries based on record timestamps, rather than clinical care-date range, and align the guidance with bulk data use.
initial_application: The historical application appears in commit fe1ee3d74919f92c159a423dd4014bac7bc9ebcd / SVN r14118, 'GF#13921 - Add note to $everything about periodic queries', which added _since and periodic-query explanatory text to the then-current Patient, Encounter, and Group $everything spreadsheet sources.
additional_context: The current core build no longer contains Patient/Encounter/EpisodeOfCare $everything OperationDefinition source files; their operation lists do not reference $everything, current narrative links to PA admin-incubator operation pages, and commit b487fdda4b removed those operation definitions from core. Later PA trackers FHIR-43373, FHIR-44604, and FHIR-44816 refine adjacent $everything narrative but do not reverse the _since update-mode semantics.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The active Group/$everything source includes the _since input, record-time semantics, server timestamp guidance, stable-query-parameter guidance, and _type input; Patient/Encounter are not current core source artifacts to edit.

related_jiras.note: Updated Patient $everything narrative for Provenance/AuditEvent and ordering, but did not change the _since update-mode semantics audited here.
Removed the single-bundle requirement from Patient $everything; related operational context but not a separate update-mode decision.
Synchronized Encounter/EpisodeOfCare $everything with Patient after FHIR-43373 and FHIR-44604; relevant to scope history but not decided in this seed audit.
